Since you loved Durmitor’s lakes-and-nature vibe, **Skadar Lake National Park (Montenegro)** is a great next match: it’s described as the *largest lake on the Balkans* with *very rich cultural and historical assets*, plus excellent birdlife and hiking/marked paths. [wv-8631] [wv-8633]  
If you’d rather go more into mountain scenery, **Lovćen National Park (Montenegro)** is another option with natural, cultural, and historical sights (including the Mausoleum of Njegoš). [wv-2010]
You rated **Plitvice Lakes National Park (Croatia)** the lowest, at **2/5**.

I’d recommend hiking in the **Morava Mountains near Korçë**—the guides note you can “hike to the top of the beautiful mountain Morava” and that the area offers “fantastic hiking trails” with “stunning panoramic views.” [wv-27] [wv-4227]  
If you want a different vibe, the guides also say Albania’s best-known hiking region is the **Northern Alps via Valbonë** (as an expedition destination point, alongside Vermosh, Thethi, Razëm, and Bogë). [wv-88]  
Since you’ve already been to **Thethi**, I’d prioritize **Morava (Korçë)** so you won’t repeat your trip there. [wv-88] [wv-visited:thethi]

Durmitor National Park (your highest-rated place, 5/5) includes the Tara River canyon and the Durmitor mountain range (UNESCO World Heritage). [wv-2830]  
You can focus on the lakes and natural scenery in the park’s broader landscape, since the park is organized around the canyon and mountains. [wv-2830]
